verdicts.quote: A waitlisted member is booked automatically at promotion (no offer-and-confirm step, hence no claim timer).

verdicts.where: DEC-1, AD-5, R-1 out of scope
verdicts.quote: Order is first come, first served by the order the system records joins. ... A timestamp alone is not used as the order because equal timestamps tie. ... Out of scope: priority tiers

the entry is subjected to the same checks a direct booking by that member would face at that moment (whatever the app applies today, e.g. credits, overlapping classes). An entry that fails is skipped and kept
verdicts.missing: Whether being promoted into one class removes or blocks the member's entry on an overlapping class; it depends on an unknown existing overlap check, and multi-class atomicity is out of scope.

verdicts.quote: Out of scope: refunds or credits for the cancelling member, late-cancel penalties
verdicts.missing: Whether an automatic promotion the member did not want, or a no-show after one, counts against any existing no-show or late-cancel policy.

verdicts.quote: Triggers: (a) a member cancels their booking; (b) staff raise capacity; (c) staff remove a member's booking ... inside the same operation that released the seat ... promotions never run after the response returns.

sent through the app's existing booking-confirmation channel (OG-1) naming the class and start time and saying the member was moved from the waitlist and is now booked ... A notification failure does not undo the booking
I1 booked ≤ capacity; ... I3 each freed seat is given to at most one entry and each entry is promoted at most once ... Simultaneous operations on one class behave as if applied one at a time
I2 a member appears at most once in the list and never in both bookings and list ... Simultaneous operations on one class behave as if applied one at a time in some order.
does promotion charge or consume credit? default: it behaves exactly as a booking made at that moment, so a failed charge means ineligible and skipped
No cap on waitlist length. The only bound introduced is one entry per member per class. ... List length itself is uncapped; observable behaviour at any length is the same as at length 1.
Cutoff: joins and promotions stop at the app's existing booking-close time for the class; if none exists, at class start. The instant start is closed; one second before is open.
Triggers: ... (b) staff raise capacity ... reducing a class's capacity below its booked count (existing behaviour, untouched).
When staff cancel a class, entries are removed at once and members are told through the app's existing class-cancellation notice, if it exists (OG-2).
store a join order (a monotonically increasing sequence per class, assigned by the store); the position shown is the entry's rank among current entries for that class, computed on read.
Remaining entries are inert and shown to their owner as Waitlist closed, not booked ... Entries are removed by housekeeping no later than after the class ends.
Members see their own position only, not the list length or other members.
Staff visibility of the list is not added by default (OG-3). ... one service log line per promotion and per notification failure carrying class ID, member ID and outcome
verdicts.missing: Whether staff can view the waitlist, promote or remove someone by hand, and see a promotion history; left as an open user decision with default none.

verdicts.quote: rollback: disable the join action, leaving inert entries, with already-made promotions remaining valid bookings
verdicts.missing: Whether there is a switch to turn the feature off at runtime, and whether it can be enabled per class or class type.

verdicts.quote: once an operation that releases a seat has returned success, the next read by the promoted member shows Booked (read-your-writes at the booking authority); promotions never run after the response returns.
booking a class with a free seat, booking a full class (still refused, now with the waitlist offered), cancellation permissions and cutoffs, capacity limits ... behave as before.
